prize_parts.citation: For the invention and realisation of optical lattice clocks based on magic-wavelength trapping, which brought optical atomic clocks to the 10^-18 level of fractional uncertainty

statement.case_for: I move from B018 to B015 as a single-part prize. In round 1 I ranked the lattice clock sixth only because the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize for single quantum systems seemed to cover the ground. The chair asked what would settle that for me, and Pearce, Kroll and Olsson gave an answer I accept. The comb is a ruler for optical frequencies, and Wineland's prize concerns control of single ions. Katori's idea is different in kind: a lattice at the magic wavelength cancels the light shift on the clock transition while keeping Lamb-Dicke confinement of thousands of atoms, so stability comes from many-atom averaging, not from one ion. No earlier citation describes that. From my own side, the long-standing practice of computing and then measuring spectra to understand why they look the way they do applies here: the systematic budgets at 1e-18 are tested by comparisons across species (Sr, Yb) and institutions, which is independent confirmation and not repetition of one design. The credit is the cleanest on the shortlist, Katori for the concept and first strontium lattice clock and Ye for taking performance to the accuracy frontier. I would word the citation around the magic-wavelength lattice and the achieved accuracy, not around combs or optical clocks in general.
statement.case_against: The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes has been answered but not removed, and a sceptical reader of the citation could still see a refinement of a heavily honoured line. Two names do not represent SYRTE (Lemonde), PTB (Lisdat), NIST, or the JILA co-workers (Ludlow, Bloom, Lemke, Hinkley), and I cannot verify from the supplied material how separable those contributions are. The redefinition of the second has not happened. I treat that as a metrology-body decision and not a scientific doubt, but it does mean the application milestone is still ahead. Finally, I am setting aside a case I still think is conceptually the deepest in condensed matter. B018 introduced band topology with a Z2 invariant as an organising principle, had a prediction followed by observation and roughly two decades of replication, and the 2016 citation did not cover the quantum spin Hall effect or three-dimensional topological insulators. I drop it because the credit cannot be drawn defensibly with three names: Mele and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are left out, and whether the third name is Hasan or Xue is unsettled among us.

responses.point: Pearce answered my round-1 objection by saying the comb is a tool for measuring optical frequencies, that the 2012 prize concerned manipulating single quantum systems, and that no earlier citation describes the magic-wavelength lattice, while agreeing the citation must not read as a return to combs.
responses.response: This is the argument that moved me. I accept that the lattice clock resolves a specific conflict, long interrogation of many atoms against light shifts, which neither earlier prize addressed, and that its stability is a many-atom property. I also take your request that the committee look at the inter-laboratory comparison data directly and not on trust, since independence of the 1e-18 budgets is what justifies calling this confirmed. Where I still disagree is that I would keep your admission that other groups made real first demonstrations on the record in the discussion. The citation should say what Katori's concept and Ye's accuracy work each established, so that the two names read as a deliberate allocation and not as a convenient cut.

responses.point: Kroll argues that the comb is a ruler and the lattice clock a separate scheme for the atomic reference, that international comparisons make the 1e-18 claim robust, and that a topological prize is only as strong as the credit the committee can defend, which he judges unsettled for B018 and B003.
responses.response: I agree on both the architecture and the credit, and on the topological credit you are right against my own preferred choice: I could not state in a sentence why Mele and Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are outside the prize while Hasan or Xue is inside. Your disclosure of a research stay in Hall's laboratory, with which Ye is associated, should be recorded as Pearce asks. I do not think it changes the scientific case, because six members reached B015 on attribution and confirmation, but it is right that it is in the minutes and that your support is read with it in view.

responses.point: Danielsson keeps B014 first as a discovery of nature in the plain sense, but says that if clean attribution outweighs breadth of discovery, B015 should be preferred.
responses.response: I share your regard for the diffuse flux and I ranked B014 as an alternative. The diffuse flux is a real discovery. Source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane) is statistically modest, and a collaboration of hundreds with AMANDA and DUMAND antecedents, together with Kowalski, Klein and Waxman, makes any two-name cut hard to defend. That is a different difficulty from the one I had with B018, but the practical outcome for this year is the same. You gave the condition yourself, and I think it applies. I would not call B014 weaker science. I would keep it as the strongest candidate for a later year, once the committee can say what the citation covers and whether KM3NeT and Baikal-GVD confirm it independently.

responses.point: Olsson moved from topological insulators to B015 because of attribution, keeps B018 as her first alternative, and argues against bundling the quantum anomalous Hall effect into B018 by replacing Hasan with Xue.
responses.response: I agree that B018 is the cleaner single statement of one discovery than B003, because replacing Hasan with Xue removes the first three-dimensional topological insulator observation, and I withdraw the idea that the two are interchangeable. We are in the same place on the Mele question. I would add that the first-principles band-structure work that turned the Z2 concept into a materials search is a real part of the field's strength and is credited to nobody on any of these lists, which is a further reason I would not defend any three names on the topological side this year. If the committee returns to the topic, B018 is where I would start.

responses.point: Lindroth asks that the citation stay anchored on the clock concept and its accuracy, resists using the redefinition of the second as a justification, and notes that the many-body and spin-exchange extensions of Ye's later work should not be the reason for the prize.
responses.response: I agree on all three points and would put them in the citation drafting. The lattice concept and the demonstrated accuracy should carry the prize, and the redefinition of the second and the quantum-gas extensions should be absent from it. That keeps the citation within what has been shown and avoids arguments about Sr versus Yb.

uncertainties: Whether the lattice clock is distinct enough from the 2005 and 2012 prizes in the eyes of the wider academy. I am persuaded, but I came to this view from the exchange and not from independent knowledge of the clock literature.
Whether Katori and Ye fairly cover a field in which SYRTE, PTB, NIST and the JILA co-workers made first demonstrations that I cannot verify here.

Whether a prize on topological insulators this year would have been the better use of the slot if a credit line could be agreed, and whether the Z2 prediction and its first observation are now unlikely to be recognised in a form that includes Mele.

How much my earlier preference for B018 and B007 came from my own electronic-structure background, and whether my move to B015 is a corrective or only a response to the number of colleagues who prefer it. I have tried to rest it on the architecture and attribution arguments, not the count.
statement.conflict_note: I have no documented personal or institutional connection to Hidetoshi Katori, Jun Ye or any other credited name in B015, B018 or B014. I work in theoretical electronic structure and magnetism at Uppsala, which is close to the topological-materials and DMFT candidates, so my earlier support for B018 and B007 may have carried a field-proximity bias; B015 is outside my field and I have no recusal issue. I note Kroll's disclosed research stay in Hall's laboratory and support recording it formally, as Pearce asks, and Johansson's WACQT roles on B039, which are not part of my configuration.
